case_analysis.thread_summary: This thread (February 22-25, 2025) covers a proxy Bluetooth SIG registration for Paramount Bed's 'toilet sensor' product, which the company acquired via business transfer from NEC Platforms (NECPF). Nagase (Paramount Bed) asks to carry over NECPF's prior SIG registration info (referencing NECPF's Compliance Folder DID) for a new registration under Paramount Bed's brand, targeting an April 1 sales launch. The consultant (Sakai) reviews the submitted quote request and proxy registration confirmation forms, explains the SIG registration deadline rule (must register by the date of any third-party disclosure - press release, preview event, website, dealer pamphlets - not just the sales date) and the Qualification Fee USD remittance timing (one day before the registration operation). Sakai also answers a detailed question about which model name(s)/product codes to register given the product is sold under 9 catalog codes representing different unit+bracket combinations versus 1 internal unit code, explaining the nameplate-match requirement and prohibition on wildcard/series registration. Sakai provides a fee breakdown (proxy registration support fee referencing Multi-Design, ¥250,000; Compliance Folder creation fee, ¥150,000) and the required Compliance Folder materials, then instructs sales (Iida) to issue the formal quote. A final message confirms registration completion, Compliance Folder CD-R shipment via Click Post with tracking, retention/audit guidance, and free derivative-model registration via Manage Submitted Products.
all_questions_found: Can we reuse a prior brand owner's (NECPF's) existing SIG registration information when registering an acquired product line under our own brand?
By when do we need to complete registration and remit the registration fee, given our planned April 1 sales launch?

Which model name(s)/product codes should be registered in the Product List - our 9 catalog/order codes or our 1 internal Bluetooth-unit code - and can we do a wildcard 'series' registration for future variants?
What is the cost breakdown for this registration and Compliance Folder, and what is the overall process and required materials?
Now that registration is complete, how is the Compliance Folder delivered, how long must we keep it, and do future derivative models need a new registration?
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The registration referenced a prior owner's (NECPF's) existing SIG registration and Compliance Folder ID (DID) for a business-transfer scenario. The SIG registration deadline was tied to the earliest third-party disclosure event (press release, preview event, website announcement, dealer pamphlet distribution), not simply the sales launch date, with Qualification Fee USD remittance required one day before the registration operation. For Product List model naming, the rule is an exact match to the physical product's nameplate: if 9 catalog codes (each combining the Bluetooth unit with a different mounting bracket) appear on the nameplate, all 9 must be registered; if only the single internal unit code appears, only that one is registered - and wildcard/series registrations are prohibited. The quote comprised a proxy registration support fee (Multi-Design reference, ¥250,000) and Compliance Folder creation fee (¥150,000), with required materials being the Bluetooth section of the operation manual, block diagram, and outline drawing (reuse of NECPF's prior materials permitted). After finalization, the Compliance Folder (CD-R) was shipped via Click Post with tracking, with 1-year post-discontinuation retention, audit-only presentation, and free derivative-model registration via Manage Submitted Products for future models sharing the same module/host stack.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: Business-transfer registrations were handled by accepting the prior owner's registration/Compliance Folder reference as a baseline and verifying the new brand's quote request and confirmation forms against it. Registration deadlines were derived from the earliest planned public-disclosure event rather than the sales date alone. Product List model naming was determined strictly by what appears on the physical product's nameplate, with no wildcard/series shortcuts permitted. Fee quoting separated proxy registration support (by design-reference schedule) from Compliance Folder creation, with required materials specified upfront and reuse of prior materials allowed. Post-registration, Compliance Folder delivery and retention/audit guidance were paired with proactive information about free derivative-model registration.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Misjudging the registration deadline against only the sales date (ignoring earlier disclosure events like press releases or pamphlet distribution) could cause non-compliant public disclosure before registration. Registering the wrong model name(s) (e.g., only the internal code when multiple SKU codes appear on the nameplate, or attempting a wildcard series) could leave actual sold products unregistered. Unclear fee/material communication could delay Compliance Folder delivery or surprise the customer with unanticipated costs. Failing to mention free derivative-model registration could cause unnecessary full re-registration costs for future models.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: For business-transfer acquisitions of an already-registered product, accept the prior owner's registration/Compliance Folder reference as a starting point and verify the new forms against it. Always determine the SIG registration deadline from the earliest planned third-party disclosure event, not just the sales launch date, and require Qualification Fee remittance one day ahead of the registration operation. For Product List model naming, register exactly what appears on the physical product's nameplate (all SKU codes if all are shown; only the internal code if that's all that's shown), and never use wildcard/series entries. Provide a clear fee breakdown (registration support + Compliance Folder creation) and required materials list upfront, allowing reuse of prior-owner materials where applicable, and proactively explain free derivative-model registration via Manage Submitted Products after finalization.
